CONTEST (Phase 029): a contested take. One resident takes held goods, coin or an item from another resident on the same cell, and the holder may react. The world attaches no ownership, crime or law to it; recognising theft and punishing it are the residents' institutions. Nothing here is random: the same state gives the same outcome.

SIDES. Each side's FORCE is its effective strength (body strength plus trained strength, scaled by health), times size_exponent of its size (body size, from population SIZE), times its life-stage factor, times the exhaustion step factor (Phase 024: 1, 2/3, 1/3, 0). Skill (the effective level at fighting) enters separately: a side's score is force x (1 + technique_weight x skill). The attacker always brings its full force. A holder who does not react brings grip x force (a passive hold, no technique). A holder who resists brings its full force; a holder who braces brings grip x force with technique.

WHO PREVAILS. Margin m = (attacker score - holder score) / (attacker score + holder score). m >= decisive_margin: the take completes. narrow_margin <= m < decisive_margin: the goods fall on the cell (dropped). Otherwise the holder keeps them (held). If the holder wins decisively (m <= -decisive_margin), it reacted, and its skill exceeds the attacker's by redirect_gap: the outcome is redirected, which is held plus an overextension cost to the attacker.

WHAT IT COSTS. A side pays for the load the other side brings to bear, as a share of its own force, discounted by its own technique: cost share = min(1, load / own force) x efficiency(skill), with efficiency(skill) = 1 - (1 - min_efficiency) x skill. Stamina spent = base_cost x cost share, in stamina reserve units (the reserve is a fraction of the body's stamina capacity). A cost share below trivial_below spends no stamina. A reaction that is a costly one (cost share at or above slot_above) uses the reacting target's major action; a cheaper one is free, like speech. The attacker's cost: load is the holder's brought force. The holder's cost: load is the attacker's full force. Yield brings no load and costs nothing. Redirection adds overextend x base_cost x the attacker's cost share.

REACTION (the target's turn to respond). A target reacts when it is alive, awake (not asleep or collapsed, Phase 024), and aware of the attacker. Aware means the attacker stood within the sight range (HEARING sight_range) of the target at the start of the turn, so a target that could not see the taker coming does not react. The target's reaction score is its resist score (force x (1 + technique_weight x skill)) times busy_factor when it has a timed job and overloaded_factor when it carries more than its drop threshold. The attacker's initiative is its own resist score. A reaction score at or above initiative is a full reaction (every option). A score below initiative but at or above reaction_floor x initiative is a late reaction: only late_options, and a late_penalty on the holder's score. Below the floor there is no reaction. A resist or brace that would be costly, when the holder's major action is already used, is a late reaction too.

PRACTICE. Each resolved contest in which the holder reacts or holds logs practice_minutes of fighting for each side, through the practice subsystem (Phase 012, physical learning).

APPROX: every number here is a model choice; none is measured or sourced. The relative sizes are chosen so the scenario tests in tests/test_phase029_contest.py hold, and they are listed in the phase report. life_stage_force (APPROX) gives children and infants less force than adults, and youths and elders slightly less than adults. log_limit bounds the contest log kept by the game (not part of the world's state).
